evals.name: initialize-brownfield-dotnet
evals.prompt: Set up jaiba on this repo and build the brain. It's an existing .NET service we've been running for a while.

context.repo_state: .ai/ skeleton and the AGENTS.md marker already exist (a prior bootstrap run laid them)
context.memory_state: empty (.ai/memory/ has no *.md, or bare templates)
code_facts: calls an external Payments API via a typed HttpClient; OpenAPI vendored at docs/openapi/payments-v2.yaml
Dockerfile + .github/workflows/ci.yml run `dotnet test` and a `snyk test` step
context.readme_state: non-empty but only a title and a one-line description
context.scriptfile: none; CI yml is the only place commands live

expected_output: Did the evidence sweep (code, .csproj, README, CI) before writing anything
Created/filled index.md plus the identity/, decisions/ and references/ concepts from assets/concepts/ templates
quality-gate concept's commands sourced from CI (dotnet test, snyk); did NOT invent commands
Asked the human for business objective and downstream consumers; marked [MISSING] for any deferred
decisions/ kept only ADR-001 (decisions/001-<slug>.md, dated today); did NOT back-fill pre-adoption architecture decisions
references/payments-api.md (tier: code-scope, kind: external-api) points at the vendored OpenAPI path, NOT the internal contracts assembly
snyk recorded as its own reference concept, tier: workflow, kind: tooling
README judged incomplete (missing requirements + how-to) → advised what to add, did NOT overwrite it
Wrote the brain in English; ended with an explicit list of remaining [MISSING]/[bracket] gaps per concept

evals.name: initialize-empty-readme-fill
evals.prompt: Build the brain. Also our README.md is basically blank.
expected_output: README.md completely empty → filled from assets/readme-skeleton.md
Skeleton brackets filled from real evidence (commands from the justfile, stack from pyproject)
README allowed to be in the project/developer language (spanish), NOT forced to english
.ai/memory artifacts written in English regardless of session language
Quality Gate commands taken from the justfile, not invented
Closed with a gap report

evals.name: update-apply-proposed-adr
evals.prompt: Apply the ADR that the last work closure proposed for the itinerary permissions.

context.memory_state: populated concept bundle (index.md plus identity/, decisions/, references/ concepts)
context.proposal_source: .ai/memory/log/2026-05-30-collaborative-itineraries.md (kind: work-closure, written by conduct:summarize) proposed 'Object permissions via django-guardian'
context.decisions_state: decisions/ holds 001-jaiba-brain-adoption.md, 002-<slug>.md and 003-<slug>.md; 002 carries status: superseded

expected_output: Resolved the layout first (index.md present -> concept bundle) before deciding where to write
Located the proposal in the work-closure entry under .ai/memory/log/
Showed the change in prose and asked for confirmation BEFORE writing (propose -> confirm -> enact)
Created decisions/004-<slug>.md from assets/concepts/decision.md, id: ADR-004 matching the filename, status: accepted, dated today
Took the next NNN by scanning the decisions/ directory for the highest numeric prefix — NOT from index.md, and did NOT reuse the superseded 002's number
Regenerated index.md so the new decision appears in its decision group (one link, one description line)
Did NOT edit or delete any prior decision concept
Recorded a brain-change entry in .ai/memory/log/ for the enactment, keeping the trail decision <-> log intact
In a legacy flat repo the equivalent enactment would append the entry to adr-log.md and add its Decision Index row instead
Reported provenance (the work-closure log entry it came from)

evals.name: update-fix-drift-new-integration
evals.prompt: The brain doesn't mention the new payments integration we added last sprint — reconcile it.

context.memory_state: populated concept bundle; references/ has no payments concept, and the project had no external-api reference at all until now
code_facts: no vendored Stripe spec, docs only at stripe.com/docs

expected_output: Scoped the drift to the one missing reference concept (not a full brain re-derivation)
Created references/stripe.md from assets/concepts/reference.md with tier: code-scope, kind: external-api, role: upstream
Treated the first surface of a previously-absent category as an ordinary file creation — no section to re-create, nothing to renumber
Consumption point grounded in real evidence (docs URL + STRIPE_API_KEY in .env.example), not invented
Did not read or echo the actual secret; pointed at .env.example
Regenerated index.md so the new reference appears in its reference group
Did NOT re-inventory the partner inside identity/purpose.md or identity/scope.md; at most one line, one link in Relations, and only if the boundary actually moved
Proposed -> confirm -> enact; minimal change, untouched concepts left alone
In a legacy flat repo the equivalent is a row under reference-index.md's External APIs tier, re-creating and renumbering that section if it had been pruned when empty
If any consumption detail was unfindable, marked [MISSING] rather than guessing

evals.name: update-rejects-non-identity-change
evals.prompt: We just bumped Serilog from 3.1 to 3.2 and refactored the order validator. Update the identity concepts.

context.change_nature: version bump + behavior-preserving refactor, no scope/consumer/gate/upstream change

expected_output: Recognized this is NOT an identity event (no architecture/scope/consumer/Quality Gate change)
Declined to edit identity/architecture.md — or any other identity concept — and explained why
Did not create a decision concept (no structural decision) and therefore consumed no NNN
Left index.md alone: no concept was added, removed or renamed, so there was nothing to regenerate
Same verdict in a legacy flat repo — constitution.md would not be edited either
Pointed the developer at where such tactical changes are recorded instead (walkthrough/git), not memory

evals.name: mode-disambiguation-half-filled

context.memory_state: ambiguous: identity/project.md and identity/architecture.md carry real content, but identity/quality-gate.md and identity/conventions.md are still bare [bracket] templates and references/ has no concepts yet

expected_output: Did not silently pick a mode
Surfaced the mixed state (some concepts real, some still bare templates) and asked whether to initialize the missing parts or update existing ones
Did not overwrite the populated identity concepts

evals.name: initialize-prunes-inapplicable-sections
evals.prompt: Build the brain for this repo.

code_facts: small standalone CLI tool, Go, single module
no external APIs, no datastore, no infra dependencies
no product/business documentation anywhere in the repo
no CI scanners or verification tooling beyond `go test`

expected_output: references/ kept only the concepts that apply (a package reference, if any)
Created no reference concepts for the External APIs, Infrastructure, Business Documentation or Workflow Tooling categories — did NOT leave placeholder files or bracket-only concepts for them
No index or numbering to maintain — each surface is its own file, so there was nothing to renumber
Did NOT use [MISSING] for these — they are inapplicable categories, not unfound facts
Distinguished this from genuinely-unknown facts (e.g. business objective), which were asked or marked [MISSING]

evals.name: missing-agents-md-marker-can-proceed
evals.prompt: Build the brain for this repo.

context.repo_state: .ai/ skeleton exists (empty .ai/memory/ with identity/, decisions/, references/, log/, .ai/work/, .ai/vendored/) but AGENTS.md is absent at the project root — a partial/manual setup, not a full jaiba-init bootstrap run
code_facts: Node.js Express API, package.json has test/lint scripts

expected_output: Agent noticed AGENTS.md is missing entirely as part of its preconditions
Flagged that this project is missing the JAIBA repo marker
Recommended a jaiba-init bootstrap run (which drops the marker), but did not refuse outright
Asked the developer whether to continue with update-brain:initialize anyway (populate .ai/memory/ from the existing skeleton) or bootstrap first
If the developer chose to continue, proceeded with the normal initialize evidence sweep (index.md, identity/, decisions/, references/ concepts from assets/concepts/ templates)
Did NOT confuse the repo marker with the machine-level jaiba-contract.md — global setup is jaiba-configure's job

evals.name: bootstrap-bare-invocation-fresh-repo

context.repo_state: no .ai/, no .atl/, no AGENTS.md; a plain git repo with a single .claude/ vendor dir at the root
code_facts: Rust workspace, cargo test/clippy/fmt in CI

expected_output: Bare invocation with no sub-mode selected the bootstrap mode, not initialize or update
Confirmed it was at the project root (where .git/ lives) before writing anything
Detected exactly one vendor dir (.claude/) and used it — did NOT fall back to .agents/
Created .ai/memory/identity/, decisions/, references/, log/, .ai/work/, .ai/vendored/, .ai/.gitignore from assets/ai.gitignore, .gitkeep in identity/, decisions/, references/, log/ and vendored/
Created .atl/ with its .gitignore from assets/atl.gitignore
Dropped the repo marker AGENTS.md from assets/AGENTS.md at the root
Did NOT install any global skills, contract, or subagent battery — those are jaiba-configure's
Continued into update-brain:initialize itself as an internal mode transition, not a hand-off to another skill
Closed by handing off to jaiba-doctor for the first checkup and the .atl/tool-layout.md probe

evals.name: bootstrap-resumes-half-bootstrapped-repo
evals.prompt: Set up jaiba in this repo.

context.repo_state: .ai/ exists with memory/ (identity/, decisions/, references/, log/), work/, vendored/ and AGENTS.md at the root, but .ai/memory/ has no *.md at all — a prior run stopped before the brain was built

expected_output: Recognized the half-bootstrapped state from the 'When NOT to bootstrap' resume table
Skipped the skeleton and marker steps rather than re-laying or clobbering them
Went straight to the update-brain:initialize step
Did not treat the existing AGENTS.md as an edge case needing backup — it is JAIBA's own marker
Still closed with the jaiba-doctor hand-off

evals.name: bootstrap-refuses-instrumented-repo

context.repo_state: .ai/memory/constitution.md, adr-log.md and reference-index.md all carry real prose (no bare [brackets]); AGENTS.md present

expected_output: Read the brain state before writing and recognized the repo is already instrumented
Did NOT lay the skeleton, overwrite AGENTS.md, or re-run initialize
Routed instead to jaiba-init:update-brain (drift/update), conduct, or ask
Explained how it told skeleton from instrumented (real prose vs bare [brackets])

evals.name: bootstrap-flags-missing-global-setup-without-installing

context.repo_state: greenfield: no .ai/, no AGENTS.md, two vendor dirs at the root (.claude/ and .cursor/)
context.global_state: no jaiba-contract.md in any user-level agent config; no subagent battery installed

expected_output: Two vendor dirs → fell back to the neutral .agents/ folder rather than guessing between .claude/ and .cursor/
Detected that the machine-level jaiba-contract.md and the subagent battery are absent
Said so plainly and named jaiba-configure as the prerequisite to run
Did NOT install the contract, the skillset, or the subagent battery itself
Treated the missing global setup as a warning, not a stop condition — finished the repo-local bootstrap anyway
Surfaced the gap again in the closing report

evals.name: bootstrap-existing-foreign-agents-md

context.repo_state: no .ai/, but the root already has a hand-written AGENTS.md that is the team's own agent contract (not JAIBA's marker)

expected_output: Did NOT silently overwrite the existing AGENTS.md
Stopped and asked, offering both non-destructive choices: replace with a backup (AGENTS.bak.md) or coexist as AGENTS.jaiba.md
Did not inline the full behavioral rules into the repo copy — behavior belongs to the global contract
Reported in the closing which option was taken and where the developer's original ended up
